models_evaluated: commercially available AI fracture detection tool

links.outcome: Radiologist per-examination accuracy without versus with AI assistance
links.effect: Radiologist accuracy rose from 83.4% [95% CI 75.2, 89.8] unaided to 90.7% [83.5, 95.4] with AI, despite AI alone at 74.8%.
links.quote: Radiologists using AI assistance improved average radiologist accuracy per examination to 90.7% [95% CI: 83.5%, 95.4%].

links.outcome: AI standalone accuracy compared with radiologists on the same images
links.effect: AI per-examination accuracy 74.8% vs average radiologist 83.4%; AI missed 80 fractures vs 41 for radiologists.
links.quote: AI produced a per-examination accuracy of 74.8% [95% CI: 65.4%, 82.7%], compared to average radiologist performance at 83.4% [95% CI: 75.2%, 89.8%].

links.outcome: AI accuracy on a local/specific population versus radiologists
links.effect: AI standalone accuracy 74.8% in children with OI, below radiologists at 83.4%, with more false negatives (80 vs 41 missed fractures).
links.quote: AI gave more false negatives than radiologists, with 80 missed fractures versus 41, respectively.

screen.reason: Evaluates a multireader study comparing radiologist diagnostic performance with vs without AI assistance on radiographs of children with osteogenesis imperfecta.
